topic.title: $1 billion is 250 whole working lives at $100,000 a year

title: To earn a billion, start 10,000 years ago ⏳
description:
How long would a good salary take to earn one billion dollars?
An animated story with illustrative numbers; the characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.
cta: When would you have had to start? Comment

lines.text: A billion dollars on a good salary. When would you have to start?
Here's the game. You earn $100,000 a year and never spend a cent. Let's walk back through time until the pile reaches $1 billion.
One whole career of hard work adds up to $4.0M. That's a great life, and it's nowhere near the goal.
To reach $1 billion, you'd need 10,000 years of that salary. That's 250 whole careers, back to back.
So rewind the clock. Past the moon landing, past the Colosseum, past the pyramids, and keep going, to the end of the last ice age, when people hunted mammoths.
So nobody gets a billion from a salary? Then how do billionaires get there?
Because they don't get paid by the year. They own a piece of something that grows, like a company, so the pile grows even while they sleep.
That's the gap. A salary adds $100,000 a year, while a big fortune can move by more than that in a single minute.
So to get a billion on my salary, when would I have needed to start?
